title: K6 telephone kiosk, Sir Giles Gilbert Scott, 1935

subject.summary: The K6 cast-iron telephone kiosk designed by Sir Giles Gilbert Scott in 1935 for the General Post Office's Silver Jubilee, as the survivors stand in Britain: red-painted, 2.51 m tall on a 0.92 m square plan, three glazed sides with eight strips of three panes, a solid rear panel, an illuminated TELEPHONE sign and embossed crown on each of four arched pediments, and a shallow domed roof.

identity.feature: Long horizontal glazing: eight strips of three lights on each of three sides, a wide central pane with narrow margin lights
An arched pediment carrying an embossed crown above an illuminated TELEPHONE sign, repeated on all four sides
Shallow domed roof with a convex moulded edge over four segmental pediments
Cast-iron corner posts, plinth and cornice, with a teak door hung on an outward hinge and a cup handle
Solid cast rear panel with a sunk moulded panel and the foundry plate at its foot
